questions.prompt: After NRSC v. FEC (June 2026), how much can a party spend in coordination with its Senate nominee?
options: Up to a set limit per state
questions.why: The Supreme Court struck down the limits on party coordinated spending, so parties can now spend without limit alongside their candidates.

questions.prompt: Does a 501(c)(4) nonprofit that runs election ads have to disclose its donors?
questions.why: It must report the ad spending, but generally not its donors unless they gave for that ad. That's why it's called dark money.

questions.prompt: How often do House and Senate campaigns file their regular reports in an election year?
questions.why: Candidate committees file quarterly, plus 12 days before and 30 days after each election. Monthly filing is only an option for PACs and parties.

questions.prompt: HMP (a super PAC) has spent $5.6M in PA's 1st District House race. Which party is it helping?
questions.why: Its spending supports the Democrat or attacks their opponent. Every group's filings list who it backs or opposes.

questions.why: Outside money and candidate money point opposite ways here: the Republican leads fundraising by $1.5M.
